title: Cambridge IELTS 20 Academic Listening Test 2 Part 1
description: Đoạn hội thoại phỏng vấn chăm sóc người cao tuổi chuẩn đề thi Cambridge IELTS 20 Test 2 Part 1.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (1)
lines.text: Test two.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (2)
lines.text: This is the IELTS listening test.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (3)
lines.text: You will hear a number of different recordings, and you will have to answer questions on what you hear.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (4)
lines.text: There will be time for you to read the instructions and questions, and you will have a chance to check your work.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (5)
lines.text: All the recordings will be played once only.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (6)
lines.text: The test is in four parts.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (7)
lines.text: At the end of the test, you will be given ten minutes to transfer your answers to an answer sheet.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (8)
lines.text: Now turn to part one.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (9)
lines.text: Part one.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (10)
lines.text: You will hear a woman who is caring for her elderly mother talking to a friend.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (11)
lines.text: First, you have some time to look at questions one to four.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (12)
lines.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions one to four.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (13)
lines.text: It's really good to see you, Tom.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (14)
lines.text: Since I had to give up work, I feel I'm losing touch with my friends and colleagues.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (15)
lines.text: We really miss you in the office.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (16)
lines.text: We were all so sorry you had to leave, but you must be relieved to have more time to look after your mother.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (17)
lines.text: How is she?

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (18)
lines.text: Well, she's very cheerful, but she needs a lot of help.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (19)
lines.text: Have you tried to get any support from the local council?

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (20)
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (21)
lines.text: I didn't know I could.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (22)
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (23)
lines.text: They offer different kinds of practical support.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (24)
lines.text: They realize that carers sometimes need time for all the other responsibilities they have apart from the person they're caring for, and also that they sometimes need a break.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (25)
lines.text: Absolutely.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (26)
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (27)
lines.text: So tell me more.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (28)
lines.text: How do I go about getting this support?

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (29)
lines.text: Well, you'd have to have an assessment of your mother's needs.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (30)
lines.text: That means someone would come round and talk to you about the situation and what you need.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (31)
lines.text: So for a start, they'd want to know the amount of time you spend looking after your mother every day.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (32)
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (33)
lines.text: Then they'll probably ask you what sorts of tasks you do for your mother during the day, things like if she needs help with getting dressed, for example.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (34)
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (35)
lines.text: I help her with that, and also I help her get into the shower in the morning.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (36)
lines.text: Yes, that sort of thing.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (37)
lines.text: They'll probably ask you if you do the shopping for her and help her at mealtimes, and whether she can cope using money.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (38)
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (39)
lines.text: That's becoming a bit of a problem.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (40)
lines.text: She used to be very good at it, but not anymore.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (41)
lines.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions five to 10.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (42)
lines.text: Now listen and answer questions five to 10.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (43)
lines.text: And be ready to tell them about anything you find particularly difficult about caring for your mother.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (44)
lines.text: So recently, I've noticed she started to have quite bad problems with her memory.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (45)
lines.text: If I wasn't there, I think she'd forget to eat, for example, and often she doesn't seem quite sure what day it is.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (46)
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (47)
lines.text: Tell them about that.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (48)
lines.text: And are there any physical difficulties you have caring for her?

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (49)
lines.text: Lifting her, for example.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (50)
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (51)
lines.text: She's quite heavy, and I'm afraid of hurting my back.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (52)
lines.text: I'd be in real trouble if that happened.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (53)
lines.text: They can give you advice about that and also about how to avoid the possibility of your mum having a fall.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (54)
lines.text: Great.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (55)
lines.text: So once they've done this assessment, if I'm eligible, what happens next?

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (56)
lines.text: Well, they might support you financially, so they might help you with transport costs, like if you have to get a taxi to take your mother for an appointment, for example.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (57)
lines.text: I usually drive her myself, actually, So could I claim for the petrol?

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (58)
lines.text: You could, and you can claim for the insurance too.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (59)
lines.text: Oh, right.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (60)
lines.text: And if you need help with the housework, they can arrange for someone to come along once or twice a week.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (61)
lines.text: And one other thing, I hope you don't mind me saying this, but it's important you look after yourself, and it seems to me you're under quite a bit of stress.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (62)
lines.text: I am.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (63)
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Speaker 3 (64)
lines.text: Well, tell the council because they may be able to give you some advice on how to minimize it.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (65)
lines.text: Really?

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (66)
lines.text: Though, actually, I feel so much better having talked to you.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (67)
lines.text: I'll get in touch with the council straight away.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2 (68)
lines.text: Now shall we go for coffee?

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (69)
lines.text: That is the end of part one.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1 (70)
lines.text: You now have one minute to check your answers to part one.
